text:
maria: quick ask — can someone run a small latency + p95 regression sweep for structured output (json schema) vs plain text for streaming and sync endpoints? want to validate the new kernel selector doesn't add overhead when we emit tool/function-like JSON.

kevin: I can take this on. which models + infra? dedicated GPU or hosted infra?

maria: thanks! prioritize: llama2-13b-q4 and a tuned 7B quant model (the two we use for smoke). run on dedicated pool (t4-reserved) and a hosted small node (a2-standard) if possible.

ashok: add KV-cache hit/miss variations — structured outputs often force repeated prefixes, so cache behavior could change latency. also test small vs long sequence lengths (128 vs 2048).

kevin: noted. do you want function/toolcall emulation too (i.e., streaming with intermittent tool tokens)? that could affect flush behavior.

maria: yes — three cases: 1) plain text, sync; 2) structured JSON output, sync; 3) streaming structured JSON (chunked tokens), and 4) streaming with simulated toolcall boundary (inserted special token stream). keep batch size 1 for latency SLOs.

sasha: can you paste the small harness or CLI? i'll try to reproduce locally for dev iterate.

maria: here's a quick run command (adapted from infra/scripts/bench/run_latency.sh):

```
# run p95 microbench for model
python bench/latency_sweep.py \
  --model llama2-13b-q4 \
  --mode streaming|sync \
  --output-schema json|text \
  --seq-len 128,2048 \
  --kv-cache on,off \
  --repeats 200 \
  --node-type dedicated,hosted
```

maria: expected metrics: p50/p95/p99 wall time, token-throughput, tail memory usage, #kernel-switch events (from tracer). attach raw logs + summary CSV.

ci-bot: pipeline triggered: bench-latency/1805012345 — queued on dedicated pool. see: https://ci.redwood/demo/bench-latency/1805012345

kevin: started the dedicated run. clocking a baseline for plain sync/text now. will push raw logs to /mnt/bench/1805012345/kevin.

ashok: small note — when measuring streaming structured JSON, add an additional check that the serializer doesn't allocate large temp buffers per token. i saw a tiny regression in a prior change.

sasha: i ran the local smoke for seq=128, kv=on. streaming structured gives ~8% higher p95 vs text on a2-hosted — looks like flush frequency. attaching snippet: `stream_flush_interval=20ms` seems to reduce gap.

kevin: dedicated results (first pass):
- llama2-13b-q4 sync/text p95=42ms
- llama2-13b-q4 sync/json p95=47ms
- llama2-13b-q4 streaming/json p95=55ms (many small writes)
- streaming+tool-boundary p95=68ms (extra serialization)
raw at /mnt/bench/1805012345/kevin/results.csv

maria: thanks — can you add kernel-switch counts? and try bumping streaming batch flush to 50ms to see impact. also note which compiler flags used.

kevin: will re-run with flush=50ms and compile flags: -O2 + kernel-priority=latency. requeueing.

ci-bot: bench-latency/1805012345 re-run queued (flush=50ms). estimated 12m.

ashok: if the 50ms flush reduces p95 substantially we should consider defaulting to slightly larger flush for structured outputs, at least until we implement aggregator-based chunking. open a short RFC if so.

sasha: good call. i'll draft a tiny ops-note explaining tradeoffs.

maria: awesome. plan: kevin finish runs, attach results + csvs, sasha draft ops-note, ashok evaluate KV-cache variance. i'll open a tracking ticket and tag y'all. :thumbsup:

kevin: copying summary here when done.

ci-bot: bench-latency/1805012345 completed — artifacts: /ci/artifacts/bench-latency/1805012345 (logs, csvs, tracer.json). status: success.

kevin: uploaded summary CSV + tracer. preliminary: flush=50ms reduced streaming/json p95 from 55ms -> 48ms, streaming+tool from 68ms -> 60ms. kernel-switch events unchanged. full writeup incoming.

maria: great, thanks everyone. next step: open PR with bench artifacts + add a short changelog entry for default flush behavior if we decide that.

sasha: will do ops-note and link the PR. :eyes:
